dataset.title: Compilation of Geospatial Data (GIS) for the Mineral Industries and Related Infrastructure of Africa
dataset.abstract: This geodatabase reflects the U.S. Geological Survey’s (USGS) ongoing commitment to its mission of understanding the nature and distribution of global mineral commodity supply chains by updating and publishing the georeferenced locations of mineral commodity production and processing facilities, mineral exploration and development sites, and mineral commodity exporting ports in Africa. The geodatabase and geospatial data layers serve to create a new geographic information product in the form of a geospatial portable document format (PDF) map. The geodatabase contains data layers from USGS, foreign governmental, and open-source sources as follows: (1) mineral production and processing facilities, (2) mineral exploration and development sites, (3) mineral occurrence sites and deposits, (4) undiscovered mineral resource tracts for Gabon and Mauritania, (5) undiscovered mineral resource tracts for potash, platinum-group elements, and copper, (6) coal occurrence areas, (7) electric power generating facilities, (8) electric power transmission lines, (9) liquefied natural gas terminals, (10) oil and gas pipelines, (11) undiscovered, technically recoverable conventional and continuous hydrocarbon resources (by USGS geologic/petroleum province), (12) cumulative production, and recoverable conventional resources (by oil- and gas-producing nation), (13) major mineral exporting maritime ports, (14) railroads, (15) major roads, (16) major cities, (17) major lakes, (18) major river systems, (19) first-level administrative division (ADM1) boundaries for all countries in Africa, and (20) international boundaries for all countries in Africa.
dataset.purpose: The primary goal of this project was to compile a range of geospatial data layers that can be used in analysis of the extractive fuel and nonfuel mineral industries and the related economic and physical infrastructure of Africa, which are integral for the successful operation of the mineral industries within the region and the transportation of mineral products across domestic and global markets.

layers.name: AFR_Mineral_Facilities Feature Class
layers.description: Geodatabase feature class containing the location of 2,408 fuel and non-fuel mineral production and processing operations in 1,866 locations across Africa compiled from a variety of sources by the U.S. Geological Survey’s (USGS) National Minerals Information Center. The dataset provides some generalized information about each mineral operation, such as name of the operation or facility, mineral commodity(ies) produced or processed, status (as of 2018), capacity, operator/ownership, and location descriptions. Non-GIS data were derived from Table 2 of individual country chapters published in the USGS 2018 Minerals Yearbook, Vol. III (Area Reports: International) publication. All data were reorganized and restructured from their original format to fit our GIS attributes table format, updated for accuracy when additional information was available, and georeferenced for this GIS using various sources that included company documents (annual reports, press releases, etc.), scientific/geologic reports, industry reports, government reports, maps, digital mapping services, and minerals- and mining-specific databases, as noted for each record. The data are intended to highlight the state of the minerals industries in Africa as of 2018. Note: for attribute field "DsgAttr07 (Annual Production Capacity)" null values (production capacity data not available) are represented by the value "-999"; for attribute field "DsgAttr09 (Capacity Notes)" "c" denotes capacity is a combination of more than one facility, "e" denotes capacity is estimated, and "g" denotes capacity is in gross weight of the commodity.

layers.description: Geodatabase feature class containing the location of selected mineral deposits of Africa published by the U.S. Geological Survey in Professional Paper 1802 and its accompanying Data Release (“Critical mineral resources of the United States—Economic and environmental geology and prospects for future supply” accessed at https://mrdata.usgs.gov/pp1802/) https://www.sciencebase.gov/catalog/item/594d3c8ee4b062508e39b332), as well as Open File Report 2005-1294 (“Reviews of the Geology and Nonfuel Mineral Deposits of the World” accessed at https://pubs.usgs.gov/of/2005/1294/). The data are intended to show the general distribution of deposits in Africa for minerals that are considered major or critical to the economy and security of the United States as of 2017. This dataset provides some generalized information about each deposit, such as feature name, deposit type, mineral commodity(ies), and location descriptions. Some entries that were inconsistent with other USGS datasets (e.g. unpublished USGS World Minerals Exploration Dataset) or duplicates across different sources were either omitted or updated if additional information was available.

layers.name: AFR_Mineral_Resources_Coal Feature Class
layers.description: Geodatabase feature class information on Africa's coal-bearing geology compiled from literature by the U.S. Geological Survey (USGS). Data are stored as polygon attributes and are intended to be used in small scale spatial investigations in a Geographic Information Systems (GIS) and as a visual aid for the discussion of Africa's coal resources. The African continent contains approximately 5% of the world's proven recoverable reserves of coal (World Energy Council, 2007). A review of academic and industrial literature indicates that 27 nations in Africa contain coal-bearing rock. Existing USGS digital geology datasets provide the majority of the base geologic polygons in this dataset. Polygons for the coal-bearing localities were clipped from the base geology that properly represented the age and extent of the coal deposit as indicated in the literature. This dataset includes information regarding the rank, age and location of coal in Africa as well as the detailed source information responsible for each coal-bearing polygon. In this feature class, the attribute field names have been modified from their original source to fit our GIS attributes table schema; descriptive field aliases were created from the original field names in the source data. This product is not appropriate for use in resource assessments of any kind.

layers.name: AFR_Mineral_Resources_Copper Feature Class
layers.description: Feature class containing information on Africa's copper-bearing geology in the form of polygons that represent permissive tracts for sediment-hosted sandstone copper deposits. The permissive tracts represent either the areal extent of, or surface projection of rocks within the upper 2 km of the Earth’s crust where undiscovered deposits of sandstone copper could be present. The dataset was created for the U.S. Geological Survey Global Mineral Resource Assessment Project (GMRAP), and published as USGS Scientific Investigations Series Report 2010-5090-Y which is part of the USGS assessment of undiscovered copper resources of the world. The primary objectives of the project are to outline the principal areas that have potential for selected undiscovered mineral resources and to estimate the probable amounts of those mineral resources to a depth of 1-3 kilometers below the earth's surface. In this feature class, all polygons that delineate permissive tracts outside of Africa were excluded, some of the original attributes were excluded or summarized, and the attribute field names have been modified from their original source to fit our GIS attributes table schema; descriptive field aliases were created from the original field names in the source data.

layers.description: Feature class containing information on the geology of the African nation of Gabon in the form of polygons that represent permissive tracts for mineral deposits. The permissive tracts represent either the areal extent of, or surface projection of rocks where undiscovered mineral deposits of the following minerals may be present: aluminum (as bauxite), gold (in alluvial and vein deposits), clay, copper, diamonds (in alluvial deposits), fluorine, iron, potassium, limestone, manganese, niobium, phosphorous, platinum-group elements (PGE), lead-zinc ± barium [Pb-Zn (Ba)], rare earth elements (REE), talc, and uranium. The dataset was created by the U.S. Geological Survey in collaboration with the Government of Gabon, Ministry of Petroleum, Gas and Mines and published by its original authors as an administrative report in the French language (see Credits section of this metadata). In this feature class, some attributes were excluded or summarized, and the attribute field names have been modified and translated from their original source to fit our GIS attributes table schema; descriptive field aliases were created from the original field names in the source data.

layers.description: Feature Class containing the power transmission lines that were completed (excludes planned and under-construction) and online in Africa in 2018. The additional classification of Ultra High Voltage (UHV) exists for transmission lines >765 kV, but as of 2018 no UHV transmission lines had been built in Africa. In several instances, lines can transmit a range of voltages that fall into more than one classification (e.g. 110/123/150 kV lines). In those instances, lines are classified based on the dominant voltage levels (e.g. 110/123/150 kV = HV; 66/88/132 kV = MV).

layers.name: AFR_OG_Resources_Recoverable Feature Class
layers.description: Feature Class containing data for cumulative production and total recoverable proven plus probable resources of conventional hydrocarbon resources in oil fields and in gas fields within Africa. Data are stored as polygon attributes, summarized by country or dependency as hydrocarbon resources in oil fields, in gas fields, in offshore fields, and total including a BOE [barrel of oil equivalent = oil + NGL + gas (BCF/6) ] (NGL = natural gas liquids). Data were derived from IHS Markit International Exploration and Production Database (accessed Feb 27, 2020), and exclude continuous resources (coalbed methane, shale gas, tight gas, shale oil, and tight oil). Units are million barrels of oil (MMBO), millions of barrels of natural gas liquids (MMBNGL), billion cubic feet gas (BCFG), and millions of barrels of oil equivalent (MMBOE). With the exception of total number of fields, data are rounded to no more than three significant digits and may not add to totals shown. Data marked "W" are withheld to conceal proprietary data. The following footnotes are included in the attributes table under the "Footnotes (MemoOther)" field: 1. Angola includes 2 oil fields in Angola/Congo Unitized Area 2. Libya includes 1 oil and 1 gas field in Libya/Tunisia JEZ (joint economic zone) 3. Nigeria includes 2 oil and 4 gas fields in Nigeria/Sao Tome and Principe JDZ (joint development zone) 4. Senegal includes 1 oil field from Guinea-Bissau/Senegal JEZ (joint economic zone) and 1 gas field from Mauritania/Senegal Unitized Area Note: IHS Markit reports less than 1000 BCFG of recoverable coal bed gas from 7 fields in the southern African countries of Botswana and South Africa. The same IHS Markit database reports less than 1000 BCFG of recoverable shale gas and tight gas from 7 fields in Algeria. Unconventional oil is limited to one oil sand field in Madagascar.

layers.name: AFR_NaturalFeatures_Rivers Feature Class
layers.description: Feature Class containing the major river systems and major artificial canals of Africa from the Natural Earth "Rivers + Lake Centerlines" geodatabase, version 4.1.0, at 1:10,000,000 (1:10m) resolution. The dataset is primarily derived from World Data Bank 2. Rivers are ranked by relative importance. Lake centerlines and minor rivers and river systems have been excluded in this layer. Major river systems, as determined by this layer's author for the purpose of this compilation, include the main trunk after which the river system is named and other significant tributaries to that system: Nile R. - includes its three main tributaries (the Blue Nile R., White Nile R., and Atbara R.), as well as the Kagera R. which forms the main tributary via L. Victoria from the headwaters of the Nile in Burundi, and the Damietta and Rosetta branches of the Nile R. in the Nile Delta. The Ismailiya Canal, connecting the Nile R. to the Suez Canal, is also included. Congo R. - includes the two main tributaries to the Congo R. (the Lualaba R. and the Chambeshi R.). Niger R. - includes the main trunk of the Niger R. as well as the Benue R., its main tributary. Zambezi R. - includes the main trunk of the Zambezi R. as well as the Shire R., an important tributary from L. Malawi. Orange R. - includes the main trunk originating in the highlands of Lesotho (named the Senqu R. within Lesotho) as well as the Vaal R., its main tributary. Limpopo R. - includes the main trunk from the headwaters of the Marico R. Senegal R. - includes the main trunk from the headwaters of the Bafing R. as well as the Baoulé-Bakoy R., its main tributary. Volta R. - includes its three main tributaries (the Black Volta R., White Volta R., and Red Volta R.) as well as the Oti R., a smaller but important tributary from Benin. Okavango R. - includes the main trunk, originating in Angola as R. Cubango, as well as the Cuito R., its main tributary. The Okavango R. terminates in the Okavango Delta, an endorheic basin with no outlet to the ocean. Madagascar - the three largest rivers of Madagascar are also included in this layer.

layers.name: AFR_Political_ADM0_Boundaries Feature Class
layers.description: Feature Class containing the country-level administrative boundaries for all African countries and dependencies from the GADM.org database, v. 3.6, downloaded via https://gadm.org/download_country_v3.html and compiled into a single feature class. For each country, additional fields were added to the attributes table, including short-form name (Name_0), long-form name (Name_1), administrative capital (Capital_0), legislative capital (Capital_1, if different), and judiciary capital (Capital_2, if different) in accordance with the U.S. Department of State’s Independent States in the World fact sheet (https://www.state.gov/independent-states-in-the-world/), as well as 2-characgter (GENC_2), 3-character (GENC_ID), and numerical (GENC_N) code designations in accordance with the U.S. National Geospatial-Intelligence Agency’s Geopolitical Entities, Names, and Codes (GENC) standard (https://nsgreg.nga.mil/genc/discovery).
